editorial.headline: Motorcycle Parts Wholesale: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale motorcycle parts and accessories are nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks this activity there.
editorial.body:
KBLI 46633 covers the wholesale trade of motorcycle spare parts and accessories. Its scope is direct: it concerns commercial trading at the wholesale level, with motorcycle parts and their accessories forming the subject of the activity. For founders, the operative distinction is equally direct—the code concerns wholesale trade in these goods. The record presents this as a defined trading activity, not a broad description of the motorcycle sector.

The activity is open across the full set of listed scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That gives the code a wide scale profile in the national classification, from Mikro through Besar. The scale question and the foreign-ownership question should nevertheless be read separately. The former identifies the business scales open to the activity; the latter determines how foreign ownership is treated nationally and, in Bali, whether PMA registration remains available at all.

Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign capital may hold the full stake in this activity at the national level. The record cites Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021 for that treatment. This is a genuine national opening, and it should be stated without dilution. Yet it is not the final answer for a business intended to register in Bali, where the record supplies a separate and decisive local position.

Bali changes the answer completely. Its status is Blocked (risk class), and the activity is marked as blocked. A foreign investor cannot register this activity through PMA in Bali today. The stated reason is that, at the Besar scale, OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope. That places it within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium, which blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA. The record locates that moratorium in May 2026. National openness is real, but it does not override Bali’s island-wide permanent PMA block.
